IPTV glossary: EPG, M3U, Xtream Codes, catch-up and more

November 19, 2026

IPTV set-up comes with a lot of jargon. Here's what each term means, and where it shows up in Tuned.

Playlists and logins

IPTV. Internet Protocol Television: TV channels, films and shows delivered over the internet instead of cable, satellite or an aerial. Tuned is a player; the channels come from your provider.

Playlist. The list of channels, films and shows your provider gives you, with a link to each stream.

M3U / M3U8. The most common playlist format: a text file starting with #EXTM3U, with one entry per channel giving its name, logo, group and stream link. M3U8 is the same thing saved as UTF-8. See adding an M3U playlist.

Xtream Codes. A kind of IPTV server many providers use. You sign in with a server address, username and password, and get live TV, films, shows, the guide and catch-up. See adding an Xtream Codes playlist.

MAC portal (Stalker, Ministra). A server made for MAG set-top boxes. Instead of a password, your provider registers your device's MAC address. See adding a MAC portal.

MAC address. A hardware ID written as six pairs of characters, like 00:1A:79:12:34:56. For a MAC portal, it's the one your provider registered.

Connections. How many streams your account may play at once. Tuned always uses one.

The guide

EPG. Electronic Programme Guide: what's on now, next and later on each channel. See setting up the TV guide.

XMLTV. The file format most EPGs come in. A "guide link" or "EPG link" is an XMLTV link.

tvg-id. The ID in an M3U playlist that ties a channel to its entry in the guide. When it doesn't match, the channel's guide is empty; see the TV guide is empty.

Watching

Live TV. Channels as they air.

VOD. Video on demand: films and shows you start whenever you like.

Catch-up (TV archive). Your provider's recordings of past programmes, usually a few days back. See catch-up.

Timeshift, or pause and rewind live TV. Pausing a live channel and going back a few minutes. In Tuned, the device keeps the last 30 minutes of the channel you're watching.

Buffering. The player waiting for more of the stream to arrive. See fixing buffering.

HLS. HTTP Live Streaming, a common way of sending video in short pieces; its playlists end in .m3u8.

TS (MPEG-TS). The format most live IPTV channels are sent in: one endless stream.

User agent. The name an app gives a server when it asks for something. Some servers only answer players they know. See changing the user agent.

Devices

Android TV / Google TV. Android for TVs. Google TV is Android TV with Google's home screen. See Tuned on Android TV.

Chromecast. Google's way of sending video from a phone to a TV. See casting.

DLNA / UPnP. An older standard many smart TVs use to play video from other devices on the same network. Tuned casts to these too.

Picture-in-picture. Android shrinking the video you're watching into a small window when you leave the app.

Frame rate matching. Switching the TV's refresh rate to the video's (24, 25, 50 or 60 frames a second) so motion looks smooth.
